question: The term 'Green Revolution' refers to the new agricultural technology developed during the 1950s and 1960s by a team of agricultural experts at the International Centre for Maize and Wheat Improvement in Mexico and at the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) in _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) is located in the **Philippines**.
 
• The Green Revolution was a period of significant increase in agricultural production due to new technologies.
 
• The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) played a pivotal role in developing high-yielding rice varieties.
 
• IRRI is headquartered in Los Baños, Laguna, Philippines.
 
• **Philippines**
 
 
• Located in Southeast Asia
 
• Capital - Manila
 
• Official languages - Filipino and English
 
• Currency - Philippine peso
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution**

 
 
• The term 'Green Revolution' refers to the large increase in crop production achieved by the use of fertilizers, pesticides, and high-yield crop varieties.
 
• It began in the 1950s and 1960s and significantly impacted global food production.
 
• Key figures include Norman Borlaug, who developed high-yielding wheat varieties.
 
• The initiative helped many developing countries achieve food self-sufficiency.
 
 
 
• **International Rice Research Institute (IRRI)**
 
 
• Founded in 1960
 
• Located in Los Baños, Laguna, Philippines
 
• Focuses on rice research to improve the health and welfare of rice farmers and consumers
 
• Develops high-yielding and disease-resistant rice varieties
 
 
 
• **International Centre for Maize and Wheat Improvement (CIMMYT)**
 
 
• Founded in 1966
 
• Headquartered in Mexico
 
• Focuses on maize and wheat research to improve food security and livelihoods
 
• Key contributor to the Green Revolution through the development of high-yielding crop varieties
